races.name: Betfred Flying Scotsman Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Varzi
runners_data.note: Won over 6f at Goodwood on good going and placed over 5f — stepping up to 7f on soft for the first time is an unproven combination for this Burke runner; the favoured draw in stall 3 is a plus but the class jump to Listed and the trip extension are significant asks for a lightly-raced juvenile.
runners_data.comment: Varzi arrives on the back of two tidy efforts — a win last time and a second two starts back — giving him strong recent momentum, and his trainer is firing at 31% over the past fortnight; the chief concern is whether 128 lb stretches his stamina over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Kach Above
runners_data.note: Back-to-back 7f wins on good going give Kach Above solid credentials at the trip, and stall 1 (strongly favoured) with Rowan Scott aboard is a tactical asset; the 49-day absence and trainer's 0-from-20 form over 14 days are mild flags, but the draw and trip form make this a legitimate place contender.
runners_data.comment: Kach Above won two of his last five starts, including back-to-back victories two and three starts back, and has run over today's trip; drawn in stall one carrying 128 lb, the chief concern is a trainer who has gone 0/20 in the last 14 days.

runners_data.name: Dandyman Dan
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard identifies Dandyman Dan as a principal danger, and his prominent style from stall 6 (neutral) gives Kevin Stott options; however, his sim-going record is 0 wins and 0 places from five soft-ground starts, which is a concrete concern when the going is officially soft, and the step back to 7f after a 3rd over that trip last time is at least proven.
runners_data.comment: Dandyman Dan shaped with real promise when third last time out, and a winner five starts back, so the form is there; he has raced over today's trip and going before, though 49 days off the track is the one query connections must answer.

runners_data.name: Engraved
runners_data.note: Sole career run was a promising 2nd over 1m on good — stepping back in trip to 7f on soft is an intriguing unknown, and James Fanshawe's 14-day strike rate of 4/17 is respectable; Daniel Muscutt rides, and the prominent style suits this scenario, though the experience gap against OR-rated rivals is real.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts, Engraved at least shapes with some promise after a second last time out, and he has run over today's trip before, but a rating of 86 ranking him seventh of nine makes him hard to fancy from stall five.

runners_data.name: Forbidden Fire
runners_data.note: A convincing debut winner over 6f on good for Balding and Murphy, but steps sharply in class here to Listed company over 7f on soft for the first time — Oisin Murphy's quality is the clear upside, while the wide draw in stall 8 (against the bias) and the soft ground are factors to weigh against the raw ability shown on debut.
runners_data.comment: Forbidden Fire won last time out and has run over today's trip, giving her a pair of positives to call on from stall eight, but a speed rating of 53 and a ranking of sixth of nine suggest she faces a stern test against stronger company here.

runners_data.name: Rock Montreal
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's debut winner over 7f on good ground enters Listed company in a single jump — the form is wholly unexposed and the trainer regularly targets juvenile races with confidence, but stall 7 (against bias) and the soft-ground unknown are genuine questions for a horse with one run under its belt.
runners_data.comment: Rock Montreal won last time out, so he arrives in form, and has run over today's trip; but ranked bottom of nine on our figures, he faces a stiff rise in class that makes him hard to fancy at these weights.

runners_data.name: Nabati
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's highest-rated runner in the field at OR 104, with a form string of 1-2-1 over six furlongs on good — William Buick's tactical intelligence from a neutral draw in stall 4 is central to the hold-up plan working, and the step to 7f on soft ground should, if anything, bring his stamina into play as the race is run at a controlled tempo behind Vega King.
runners_data.comment: Nabati arrives in fine nick, a winner last time out and again three starts back, with only a second sandwiched between; he has run over today's trip and carries 128 lb from stall four.

runners_data.name: Minkaas
runners_data.note: Showed improvement to win over 6f on good recently but faces a significant class leap into Listed company, and the wide draw in stall 9 (against the bias) is a compounding disadvantage for a hold-up horse who needs soft ground to suit — Tom Marquand is a capable pilot but the raw materials are against a winning run here.
runners_data.comment: Minkaas won last time out and has run over today's trip, but she carries 123 lb from stall nine and faces stiffer company on a rating of 79, with our rating of 95 suggesting she holds unexplored potential to offset those concerns.

runners_data.name: Vega King
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner in the race and well-drawn in stall 2 (favoured), giving Clifford Lee a clean path to the rail; the form of 4-1-0 in recent starts includes a win over 8f, confirming stamina, and his uncontested lead on soft ground will be run at a measured pace — his chance of winning is limited by the OR of 92 against stronger rivals, but he is the key pace influence for the entire field.
runners_data.comment: Ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Vega King is hard to fancy on his latest unplaced effort, and a seven-pound gap to his official mark underlines the concern; the trainer's sharp 31% strike rate over the past fortnight and experience over today's trip are the few crumbs of comfort.

races.paceDynamic: Vega King is the sole confirmed front-runner and, drawn in stall 2 (favoured), he will slot across to the inside rail and set a controlled, uncontested tempo on soft ground over seven furlongs — there is no rival with a confirmed lead role to challenge him for it. Dandyman Dan and Engraved are the prominent horses who will sit just off the pace in the early stages, with Forbidden Fire likely to be ridden positively from the wide draw in 8. Nabati (hold-up) and Kach Above (midfield, well-drawn in stall 1) will be tracking from the middle of the pack, while Rock Montreal and Minkaas operate deepest of all. A single, uncontested pace-setter on soft ground over an extended trip creates a sustainable gallop that will stretch the field gradually rather than stop-start — this fundamentally favours hold-up and late-finishing profiles who can conserve energy before delivering a sustained closing effort in the final two furlongs, giving the clear edge to deep closers with proven stamina at the trip.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Nabati Closes Powerfully
scenarios.trigger: If Vega King sets an honest but manageable pace and the race sets up as a conventional test of staying power in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Nabati, held up by Buick from stall 4, travels smoothly through the field on the soft ground and produces a sustained late challenge that his OR of 104 and class advantage underpin; his form of 1-2-1 at six furlongs points to a runner ready to be stepped up in trip and test. Kach Above, well-drawn in stall 1, picks up ground from midfield to fill the frame as the pace-setters tire.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Vega King's pace proves genuinely soft and the prominent horses conserve enough energy to kick clear in the straight.
scenarios.body: Dandyman Dan from stall 6 and Engraved from stall 5 sit just behind Vega King, and if the gallop is truly sedate those sitting off the pace get first run and grind out a result before the deeper closers can reel them in. Dandyman Dan is the stronger candidate here given his higher OR and Kevin Stott's ability to judge a pace, though his sim-going record of 0 wins from 5 on soft is a notable caveat.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Denied Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Vega King crawls and the race turns into a sprint from two furlongs out, negating hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: A falsely slow pace could leave Nabati and Minkaas with too much ground to make up when the field quickens sharply in the straight, allowing a prominent or midfield type to pinch an unassailable lead. Kach Above from stall 1, able to switch off at the front of midfield, is best-placed among the hold-up brigade to adapt, while Forbidden Fire's raw speed (sole career run: win over 6f on good) could prove decisive on a day when pure acceleration dominates over stamina.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the race falls apart tactically — multiple pace changes, traffic trouble — and an unexposed runner delivers a career-best on unfamiliar soft ground.
scenarios.body: Rock Montreal (Roger Varian, Dawson up, one career win over 7f on good) steps into Listed company on a big upgrade, and if the field strings out and provides clear daylight, his unbeaten record and Varian's knack for placing unexposed juveniles could make him a live longshot. Minkaas, also a hold-up type from a wide draw against the bias, would need the scenario to unfold perfectly but is a live each-way possibility at a price.

watchPoints.text: Nabati is the Strand top-rated selection at OR 104 — watch whether William Buick gets a smooth passage through the field from stall 4, as any traffic trouble in the straight is the primary threat to his winning chance.

Dandyman Dan's soft-ground record (0 wins, 0 places from five starts on similar going) is a concrete red flag — watch if he visibly labours once the ground begins to take its toll in the final two furlongs despite his prominent position.

Forbidden Fire is drawn in stall 8 (against the favoured low draw) — watch whether Murphy is forced wide around beaten horses in the straight, which could cost him ground and neutralise the raw speed shown on debut.

Vega King's solo role as pace-setter is critical — watch his early fractions to gauge whether the tempo is truly sustainable or if he is allowed to steal an uncontested lead that could make him harder to reel in late.

Kach Above's stall 1 draw is the best in the race — watch whether Rowan Scott takes advantage to slot in behind Vega King and get a low, ground-saving passage, which would maximise the horse's chance of producing a sustained finish at the trip he has already won at twice.

races.name: Betfred Leger Legends Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Nyman
runners_data.note: Recent soft-ground winner (1st/7f/Soft in last 5) for consistent handler Roger Fell, races from a neutral draw 9 in midfield, and a mile on this going sits well within his comfort zone; has placed twice from 11 similar-going starts so is a solid each-way participant.
runners_data.comment: Nyman bounced back from a below-par ninth with a winning return last time out and has experience of both today's trip and going, giving him a solid each-way profile at 167 lb; the concern is whether six days is enough recovery time to back that up.

runners_data.name: Masaban
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's 3yo has genuine front-running credentials and soft-ground form, drawn 10 in a neutral stall but one of two confirmed pace-setters who will force an early contest; holds a win at 8f on Good and placed on Soft, making this trip and conditions combination workable.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and a winner five starts back, Masaban has experience of today's trip and going to call on, but a mixed recent profile — including a fifth three starts back — and 156 lb from stall 10 are the checks on his chance.

runners_data.name: Berry Clever
runners_data.note: Chris Dwyer's consistent 5yo has run four consecutive fourths and rarely threatens to win despite respectable efforts; midfield operator on Good to Soft going, drawn 6 neutral, and the weight of evidence here is that she places more often than she wins.
runners_data.comment: Berry Clever has been frustratingly consistent in the wrong way, finishing fourth in four of his last six starts and yet to score, though he has experience over today's trip and going and the 13-day turnaround suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Bella Bisbee
runners_data.note: Tom Scudamore takes the ride on this prominent racer drawn ideally in stall 5 (favoured), and Scott Dixon's wider string is out of form (0/20 T14); the draw is a genuine asset but trainer confidence is a concern, with no wins in recent form.
runners_data.comment: Bella Bisbee has run over today's trip and going, and a third two starts back shows she can threaten, but sixth last time and a trainer without a winner in 20 recent runners are genuine concerns for this winless mare carrying 161 lb from stall five.

runners_data.name: Celtic Chariot
runners_data.note: Kevin & Lauren Frost's 3yo has won twice at this 8f trip on Good ground and holds stall 1 — the most favoured position in the draw — racing prominently; the Strand Scorecard identifies this horse as the top pick at medium confidence, and the pace shape strongly suits a prominent runner from the inside rail.
runners_data.comment: Celtic Chariot has back-to-back wins two and three starts back to his name, but a sixth last time out and a rating of 62 — ranking him fifteenth of sixteen on our figures — make him very hard to fancy, despite the experience over today's trip and a quick enough turnaround from stall one.

runners_data.name: Clatford
runners_data.note: Jimmy Quinn partners this confirmed front-runner from the favoured stall 2, but the 85-day absence for a trainer (Scott Dixon) running 0/20 over the last 14 days is a significant concern; likely to set the pace but may lack peak fitness to sustain it over a mile on soft ground.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked last on our figures, Clatford returns after 85 days off with a trainer who has yet to land a winner from 20 attempts in the past fortnight; experience over today's trip is the one small crumb of comfort.

runners_data.name: Little Miss India
runners_data.note: Gary Bardwell partners this hold-up specialist who has won over longer trips (10f, 12f) at the STA and is dropping back sharply in trip; drawn 4 (favoured) but racing from a hold-up position over a mile with 140 days since last run makes this a speculative entry despite the handy draw.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well down the field on our figures and absent for 140 days, Little Miss India faces a stiff task, though she has winning form in her last six starts and has run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: Espona Bay
runners_data.note: Scott Dixon's 3yo holds decent recent form (1-3-3-5-3 in the last five) and is drawn wide in stall 15 against the bias, which is a meaningful negative on this track; has won at 7f and placed at 8f, so the trip is not an issue, but the draw is costly.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and a winner two starts back, Espona Bay arrives on a handy 24-day break with experience of both today's trip and going; carrying 156 lb from stall 15, he shapes as the pick on overall profile despite a trainer who has yet to strike in recent days.

runners_data.name: Wield
runners_data.note: Joseph Parr's 3yo wears tongue-tie and races from the well-placed stall 3 (favoured) in midfield; form has dipped recently (7th, 10th in last two), but has placed at this trip on Standard and reverts to a surface that should suit.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 12 of 16 on our figures, Wield looks up against it here, though he does bring distance experience and a second last time out offers a crumb of encouragement under 156 lb from stall three.

runners_data.name: Shadow Run
runners_data.note: Scott Dixon's 3yo is a genuine hold-up horse whose natural position at the rear is compromised in this field — with so many true hold-up types and prominent horses, the runner is mapped to midfield but will find it hard to get there naturally; recent soft-ground experience is positive but the style displacement (STYLE_FIT 0.93) tempers expectations.
runners_data.comment: Shadow Run shaped with promise when second three starts back, and our rating of 76 has him as the pick of the field, yet he is winless in his last six starts and the trainer's current run of 0/20 is the main concern heading into this.

runners_data.name: Serious Look
runners_data.note: Richard Patrick rides this 6yo who has recent All-Weather form and operates as a hold-up type from stall 14 (against the bias); placed record at shorter trips, but the wide draw and distance from the favoured rail combine to make this a difficult winning scenario.
runners_data.comment: Serious Look has managed just one win in his last five starts, finishing eighth last time out, and his rating of 68 ranks him thirteenth of sixteen here, making him hard to fancy; he does have experience over today's trip and arrives reasonably fresh on 25 days' rest.

runners_data.name: Caragio
runners_data.note: Adam Kirby trains and rides this 6yo, who has a win at 6f (Good) and placed at 7f, stepping back up to 8f from a wide, unfavoured stall 11; hold-up style from an adverse draw on soft ground makes this a tough assignment despite the trainer-jockey combination.
runners_data.comment: Caragio won three starts back but has posted a sixth and fifth since, and a 89-day absence plus a hefty 161 lb to carry are the key concerns; experience over today's trip and going at least leaves conditions familiar.

runners_data.name: Tolstoy
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's 7yo wears hood (hg:h) and has declining recent form (14th, 17th at 6f), now stepping back up to a mile from a wide draw in stall 12; soft-going record is thin and the form figures offer little encouragement at this stage of his career.
runners_data.comment: Ranked second of sixteen on our ratings with a speed figure of 76, Tolstoy has run over today's trip and going and arrives fresh enough at 27 days since his last start, though he is winless in his last five starts and his trainer's current 4% strike rate is a concern.

runners_data.name: Anthropologist
runners_data.note: Sammy Jo Bell partners this 4yo who previously raced prominently (hg:p headgear flag) and goes from stall 8 neutral; trainer Michael Herrington has three winners from 18 runners in 14 days which is a positive, and this horse has placed at 7f Soft — a legitimate fringe interest.
runners_data.comment: Anthropologist has been consistent without threatening the top spot in recent starts, finishing second last time out and third two starts back, yet winless in his last six; the 161 lb burden and a ranking of tenth of sixteen make progress harder to find today.

runners_data.name: Quiet Resolve
runners_data.note: Gay Kelleway rides this 5yo prominent racer from stall 16 (against the draw bias), with placed form on Good at 8f and 9f; the unfavourable draw undermines what might otherwise be an attractive profile for this trip and ground.
runners_data.comment: Ran second last time out and has experience over today's trip and going, but a fourth three starts back and a heavy weight of 161 lb from stall 16 suggest he faces a stiff task working his way into contention from midfield.

runners_data.name: Feel The Need
runners_data.note: Michael Herrington's 6yo is a true hold-up horse whose natural position at the rear is harder to achieve in this field — accommodated in midfield on the map but unlikely to get the uncontested back-of-the-field berth it needs; drawn 13 against the bias and form figures (-20067) are discouraging.
runners_data.comment: Feel The Need has been winless in his last five starts, with a placed effort two starts back the lone bright spot in an otherwise modest recent run, and six days between runs may leave him short of peak fitness; he has run over today's trip and going before, but 161 lb from stall 13 adds further to his task.

races.paceDynamic: Clatford and Masaban are both confirmed front-runners drawn in stalls 2 and 10 respectively, guaranteeing a genuinely contested early pace over this mile on Good to Soft ground at Doncaster. Clatford draws favourably on the left rail but returns after 85 days off for a trainer (Scott Dixon) with a flat 0/20 in the past 14 days, while Masaban has recent form and soft-ground experience to press hard from the gun, meaning neither is likely to dominate unchallenged. Celtic Chariot sits prominently from the highly favoured stall 1, ideally placed to track the duel and pounce as the pace-setters tire on this testing surface, which distinctly suits horses who can race close to an honest gallop and sustain their effort rather than come from off the pace. The field also holds more hold-up types than can realistically settle at the rear — Shadow Run and Feel The Need, genuine hold-up horses, have been redistributed to midfield in the pace map because the density of prominent/front-running types ahead of them will compress the rear section, meaning true late closers face a more congested picture than the map surface suggests. This race shape — honest contested pace, soft ground, Doncaster's galloping mile — firmly favours prominent racers who can latch onto the leaders from a low draw and quicken in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Clatford and Masaban fight for the front and set a genuine honest gallop that stretches the field on the Good to Soft ground.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners cut each other's throats from the early stages, leaving horses tracking in second or third gear in the prime position to collar the leaders inside the final furlong; Doncaster's straight mile rewards this profile heavily on soft ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Masaban Dictates, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Masaban establishes clear control and gets a comfortable lead after Clatford fades or fails to sustain the pressure.
scenarios.body: Masaban, racing from a neutral draw but with soft-ground form and recent race fitness, converts front-running claims into a wire-to-wire victory as rivals struggle to close on a tiring surface; a truly run mile on Good to Soft plays to a horse that relaxes in front and doesn't over-exert early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Ground Grinds, Midfield Stays
scenarios.trigger: If the soft conditions prove more testing than expected and the pace is genuinely strong enough to flatten the field, allowing resolute midfield stayers to grind past.
scenarios.body: Horses with stamina in their profile and a history of performing on soft ground pick up the pieces as front-runners over-cook the early fractions; this mile becomes a test of fortitude rather than speed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly intense and the front rank collapses, leaving a rare opening for genuine finishers to come from the rear despite their compressed position.
scenarios.body: Caragio or Serious Look, with prior form suggesting finishing ability, benefit from an unusually strong gallop that creates space; however, with Shadow Run and Feel The Need displaced from their natural berth this scenario is structurally weakened and assigned low probability.

watchPoints.text: Celtic Chariot (stall 1) and Bella Bisbee (stall 5) are both prominent racers in the most favoured draw positions — if either settles cleanly in the slipstream of the pace-duel, they become the biggest dangers to each other in the straight.

Clatford's 85-day absence for an out-of-form stable (Scott Dixon 0/20 T14) is a significant red flag — if the horse ties up before halfway, the entire pace structure collapses and Masaban inherits an uncontested lead far more easily than anticipated.

The draw bias is sharp here: Espona Bay (15), Feel The Need (13), Serious Look (14), Quiet Resolve (16), and Caragio (11) all sit against the favoured left-rail advantage — monitor whether any manage to cross early and secure cover, or whether they are simply racing uphill from the outset.

Shadow Run and Feel The Need are genuine hold-up horses mapped to midfield due to field compression — if the pace is truly strong and gaps appear late, they carry marginal but real each-way value, though their displaced position means their chance is structurally reduced versus a race with a clear back-of-the-field berth available.

Nyman ran on soft ground to win over 7f just six days ago — watch for any signs of quick-turnaround fatigue in the closing stages, but if he travels well in midfield from stall 9, his soft-ground form makes him a legitimate place candidate.

races.name: Carlsberg Danish Pilsner Flying Childers Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Sale Shark
runners_data.note: Won last time out on Soft over 5f and boasts smart juvenile form — OR 105 and strong credentials here — but draw 1 is the widest low stall on a course where middle draws are favoured, and Oisin Murphy will need to angle across from a potentially awkward berth in a field full of prominent types.
runners_data.comment: Sale Shark wins on his latest start and was a winner five starts back, with experience over today's trip and going and a timely 20-day freshener working in his favour; at 129 lb from stall one, he is the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Carry The Flag
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore and A P O'Brien land this with a horse rated OR 112, the joint-highest in the race, though all five career runs have been on Good or Good To Soft and the step into genuinely soft ground at 5f is an unknown; draw 12 is the far extreme and making up positions from a wide stand-side position in a congested field adds a logistical difficulty.
runners_data.comment: Carry The Flag shaped with promise when second last time out and gets the trip having run over today's distance before, but a seventh three starts back and only one win in his last six starts suggest he blows hot and cold, and 129 lb from stall 12 adds to the query.

runners_data.name: In The Black
runners_data.note: Won on Good over 5f but is a natural prominent racer who cannot realistically hold that role today — the field is stacked with speed, and P J McDonald is likely to find himself shuffled back behind a wall of horses, meaning a STYLE_FIT discount applies as racing outside its comfort zone with an OR of just 86.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 11 of 12 on our figures, In The Black faces a stiff task, though she does bring a win two starts back and has run over today's trip and going before; that eighth last time out is hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Agamemnon
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope rides a horse rated OR 104 who has won over 5f on Standard and placed on Soft, giving him reasonable all-ground versatility; a midfield draw of 9 is ideal for this race shape, and his style of racing — coming from off the pace — maps perfectly onto a contested early pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Final Objective
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard's top pick at medium confidence: a confirmed front-runner at OR 107 who has placed on Soft over 6f and won over Good, with James Doyle in the plate for a small but active operation; the key question is whether he can withstand Fast Track's challenge for the lead without burning energy that he needs for the final furlong.
runners_data.comment: Final Objective arrives here in fine fettle, placed last time out and a winner two starts back, bringing distance and going experience to the table; the weight of 129 lb from stall 8 is the one factor connections will need to overcome.

runners_data.name: Crownbreaker
runners_data.note: Kevin Philippart De Foy's charge has solid 5f form, placing on Good twice, but his last run was 7th on Soft over 6f suggesting soft ground may not bring out the best; draw 10 puts him on the wrong side of the field for a horse rated OR 97 trying to compete with better-credentialled prominent types.
runners_data.comment: Crownbreaker has experience of today's distance and going, and a win three starts back shows she can find the line, but seventh last time out and an unplaced run two starts back are harder to ignore; 126 lb from stall 10 adds further test for a filly ranked midfield on ratings.

runners_data.name: Flann Sunna
runners_data.note: William Buick takes the ride for the Crisfords and this filly has back-to-back wins on Good over 6f — but 43 days off the track is the longest absence in the field and the switch to 5f Soft for the first time is two unknowns arriving simultaneously; draw 2 compounds the issue from a low wide draw.
runners_data.comment: Flann Sunna has won twice in his last three starts but our figures rank him ninth of twelve in this field, and 43 days off the track adds a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and draws stall two, but the weight of 129 lb makes this a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Tokaido
runners_data.note: Tony Piccone partners a horse whose form shows a notable fading flag in finishes and who managed only 16th on Soft over 6f last time — the one soft-ground run is a red flag, the hold-up style requires finding daylight in a traffic-heavy scenario, and Amy Murphy's 14-day record of 6/20 is context rather than a lift here.
runners_data.comment: Tokaido has winning form in recent starts — four wins in his last six — but he ranks bottom of the field on our figures and that unplaced effort last time out is the harder angle to ignore; he has run over today's trip and going, and 22 days gives him a fair break, but he faces a stiff task.

runners_data.name: Fast Track
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's front-runner has a headgear note (t = tongue tie) and has placed five times from the front over 5f Good, but OR 90 is the joint-lowest in the field and going to war with Final Objective from draw 11 across a wide track on Good To Soft is a daunting ask; Tom Marquand will need to decide whether to press or allow Final Objective to dominate.
runners_data.comment: Ranked tenth of twelve on our figures, Fast Track is hard to fancy at these weights despite a lively recent profile that includes a win and three runner-up finishes in her last six starts; she has run over today's trip before and returns on a reasonable 28-day break, but the rating gap to the field leaders is a significant obstacle.

runners_data.name: El Floridita
runners_data.note: Wears a visor (v) and has won over 5f on Good with a place on Soft — the going profile is encouraging — and draw 3 gives Rowan Scott a clean sight of racing from a middle-low berth without having to cross the field; OR 96 and a midfield style make him a quiet beneficiary if the pace scenario unfolds as predicted.
runners_data.comment: El Floridita shaped well for a second three starts back and arrives fit on 20 days' rest, carrying 129 lb from stall 3 with experience of both today's trip and going; the risk is that his two most recent starts have yielded only a sixth and a fifth.

runners_data.name: Pershaada
runners_data.note: Sean Levey has a horse rated OR 106 who has won on Good over 5f twice and placed on Soft previously, giving a reasonable claim — but last time out was 14th on Soft and 0th on the win column in similar going, which tempers confidence; draw 4 is workable but the prominent style puts her right in the potential early congestion.
runners_data.comment: Pershaada won two starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, leaving her well-placed to threaten from stall four off 126 lb; the main concern is her unplaced effort last time out.

runners_data.name: Ronson
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's stable companion to El Floridita is a hold-up horse whose best form (win over 5f Good) came from off the pace, and he has only managed 10th on Soft at 6f so the ground query is live; Alex Jary must find a clear passage through what will be a tightly bunched finishing straight for this one to make an impact.
runners_data.comment: Boasts a win and a second in recent starts but has been unplaced last time out, so he arrives needing to bounce back; has run over today's trip and going before, and 129 lb from stall 5 gives punters plenty to weigh up.

races.paceDynamic: Final Objective and Fast Track are the two confirmed pace-setters, and with five of twelve runners genuinely wanting a prominent position — Sale Shark, Carry The Flag, Flann Sunna, Pershaada and Crownbreaker all likely to push forward — the early stages will be genuinely contested rather than a controlled solo lead. On Good To Soft ground at Doncaster's straight five, that contested pace is self-defeating for the leaders but creates a rhythm that will suit horses who can sit just off the boil and finish strongly; In The Black is a true prominent type who has been mapped to midfield because the field contains more speed-side horses than can realistically hold that position, with Final Objective and Fast Track most likely to actually secure the rail and lead. The tactical verdict is clear: the congested early gallop on softened ground will bleed the speed horses dry in the final furlong, favouring runners in the Midfield-to-Prominent range who can track cover, avoid the early scrimmage, and produce a sustained late drive — horses like Agamemnon and El Floridita fit that profile, while genuine hold-up types Ronson and Tokaido will need gaps to materialise at the right moment.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Trackers Win
scenarios.trigger: If the contested early duel between Final Objective and Fast Track produces a genuinely strong gallop that softens the ground-leaders before the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Final Objective and Fast Track set an honest clip from draws 8 and 11 respectively, burning each other out on the Good To Soft surface, leaving runners who tracked in the 4th-6th position best placed to collar them; this shape directly suits prominent horses with a turn of foot rather than outright pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runners Dictate
scenarios.trigger: If Fast Track or Final Objective establishes clean early cover and the pace proves deceptively honest rather than truly burning, allowing one leader to coast through to a soft lead.
scenarios.body: One of the two pace-setters, most likely Final Objective who has the higher OR and better soft-ground form, wins the battle for the lead and settles into a rhythm that the congested prominent pack cannot disrupt; on Good To Soft five furlongs where gaps close late, a horse dictating terms can prove very hard to reel in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfielders Sweep Late
scenarios.trigger: If the contested pace is extreme enough to create a messy traffic scenario 2-3 furlongs out, allowing genuine midfield runners to thread through the tiring pack.
scenarios.body: Agamemnon from draw 9 and El Floridita from draw 3 are positioned to exploit any carnage in front, sitting comfortably off the speed and finding clear running when the prominent cluster bunches and brakes; Good To Soft on a straight five rewards a sustained gallop over a flat-out burn, and both of these horses have the profile to benefit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so extreme that the entire front half of the field ties up badly and genuine hold-up horses get a run of clear daylight in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Ronson and Tokaido are the true hold-up types here, but Tokaido carries a noted fading flag and Ronson has been beaten at shorter trips; this shape requires both ideal pacing in front and a perfectly timed run through traffic, making it the lowest-probability outcome despite soft ground theoretically assisting late runners.

watchPoints.text: Watch for scrimmaging in the first two furlongs as Final Objective (draw 8) and Fast Track (draw 11) both seek to lead from wide-ish draws while Sale Shark, Carry The Flag and Pershaada also push prominently — any clip or interference at the break could reorder the race entirely.

Carry The Flag from draw 12 is the highest-rated runner in the field but faces a significant logistical challenge: Ryan Moore must either angle across the field early or accept a disadvantaged far-wide position on a course where middle draws hold the bias advantage.

Tokaido's fading flag combined with a 16th-place run on Soft over 6f last time creates a meaningful drift risk — if Tony Piccone cannot find daylight early enough, the noted tendency to fade in the finish becomes a near-certainty on today's going.

Flann Sunna is 43 days off the track and has not encountered Soft ground in her career — William Buick's early positioning from draw 2 will signal whether connections believe she needs cover for a first-run sharpener or is ready to compete flat-out.

In The Black is effectively racing outside its natural role today: a prominent type mapped to midfield by the weight of pace in this field, meaning P J McDonald faces a difficult decision between fighting for a position the horse wants or accepting a holding role for which the horse's profile is not ideally suited.

races.name: Betfred Howard Wright Doncaster Cup Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Caballo De Mar
runners_data.note: Front-runner with Oisin Murphy aboard, but tagged as a fader in the finish and stepping up significantly in class at Group 2 level; one soft-going run returned a win but small sample, and the fade flag over this trip is a material concern.
runners_data.comment: Caballo De Mar arrives on the back of a fourth last time out, but a win three starts back underlines his ability, and experience over today's trip and going suits; our top-rated runner here at 116, he looks the one to beat off 138 lb with 21 days between runs.

runners_data.name: Winday
runners_data.note: William Buick takes the ride for Emmet Mullins on this lightly-raced three-year-old whose sole form reference is a win on Good ground at 12f — this horse's natural front-running tendencies cannot be fully expressed here as other prominent types precede it in the order.
runners_data.comment: Winday won last time out but that victory sits against a backdrop of an unplaced run two starts back, and his rating of 86 leaves him ranked bottom of the seven runners here, making him hard to fancy despite the recent winning form.

runners_data.name: Queenstown
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore partners this consistent six-year-old who won last time out and carries strong placed form in similar conditions; the Strand Scorecard's top selection and the horse whose prominent-to-tracking style meshes best with a controlled pace at Doncaster.

runners_data.name: Epic Poet
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old veteran with a modest recent form string including a last-of-six on soft ground; midfield style suits in theory but soft-going figures of 1/5 and no wins or places in that subset make this an each-way outsider at best.
runners_data.comment: Rated 115 by us against an official mark of 107 suggests Epic Poet is well treated, and he has going experience to call on having run over this ground before; the risk is that he has been winless in his last six starts, and a return to form is required.

runners_data.name: Peace Belle
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with two placed efforts in soft conditions from five such runs; Jason Hart rides for Jennie Candlish and the horse's staying pedigree over 17f suggests this longer trip could unlock a stronger finish than recent form implies.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked sixth of seven on our figures, Peace Belle faces a stiff task here; the most recent of those efforts was a second last time out, and going experience on today's surface offers at least some encouragement.

runners_data.name: Beylerbeyi
runners_data.note: Hold-up type drawn wide in stall 8 with modest form including two placed efforts in soft ground; Clifford Lee takes over and the horse's 20-day gap is fine, but a best soft-ground position of 4th suggests limited upside without a significant improvement in pace dynamics.
runners_data.comment: Beylerbeyi brings strong fitness, having run just 20 days ago, and has experience of today's trip and conditions, with his rating of 104 suggesting he holds solid claims in this field; the concern is that he has been winless in his last six starts, with a fifth last time out his most recent return.

runners_data.name: Ascending
runners_data.note: De Bromhead's seven-year-old is a genuine prominent racer whose natural racing position is compromised by the front-heavy field — the fade-in-finish flag compounds the style-fit discount, and six consecutive unplaced efforts tell their own story.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Ascending nonetheless catches the eye on his going experience and an encouraging our-rating edge of 105 that marks him out as a leading danger here; the concern is a string of moderate finishes that leaves his winning thread hard to locate.

runners_data.name: Berkshire Sundance
runners_data.note: Prominent-style stayer for Andrew Balding who returns from a 42-day break carrying headgear and two recent course-distance wins on Standard going; Good to Soft is less familiar territory and the fitness question from the break is real, but Balding's 14-day figures of 12/58 show an in-form yard.
runners_data.comment: Showed well with a runner-up finish last time out, and he has run over today's trip before, but two below-par efforts in his last three starts overall temper expectations; 42 days off adds a fitness query for this gelding carrying 133 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Caballo De Mar is the one confirmed front-runner and, with only Berkshire Sundance and Queenstown likely to press from prominent positions, the pace is unlikely to be truly searching over 2m2f on Good To Soft ground at Doncaster — a flat, galloping track that rewards relaxed, well-rated travellers. Caballo De Mar carries a fade-in-finish flag and is stepping up in distance against classier rivals, so the pace it sets is likely to be controlled and sustainable rather than punishing, creating a clean, single-file procession from the front. The field contains more naturally prominent types than the race shape can accommodate: Winday and Ascending are genuine prominent horses redistributed into a midfield mapping because Caballo De Mar, Berkshire Sundance, and Queenstown are all capable of taking that ground first, meaning Winday and Ascending will likely settle further back than ideal. This sustainable, compressed tempo over a long distance on soft ground suits a well-credentialed, prominent-to-midfield traveller who can unleash a sustained gallop in the straight rather than a sharp sprint, firmly favouring the hold-a-position, stay-on profile of a horse like Queenstown.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Queenstown Controls Prominently
scenarios.trigger: If Queenstown settles in second or third behind a controlled Caballo De Mar and uses the flat Doncaster straight to grind rivals down.
scenarios.body: Ryan Moore positions Queenstown perfectly off the moderate pace, conserving energy on the turn before unleashing the horse's known stamina in the final quarter-mile; the Good To Soft conditions reward a horse with a recent win and strong soft-ground form figures.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Staying Closers Wear Down Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is even slower than expected and the hold-up runners Peace Belle and Beylerbeyi mount sustained late challenges down the straight.
scenarios.body: Peace Belle has solid placed form in similar soft conditions and closing-style races over staying trips, and Beylerbeyi carries placed course-and-distance form that could see both arrive with energy if the leaders fade.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Caballo De Mar Front Runs And Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Caballo De Mar dictates an unusually generous, uncontested tempo and the field fails to close on the long run-in.
scenarios.body: Despite the fade-in-finish flag, Oisin Murphy's tactical intelligence could allow Caballo De Mar to steal a lead no rival seriously contests until too late on this flat track; Berkshire Sundance, fresh from a 42-day break and proven over staying trips, could also capitalise on a slow pace if the field is slow to respond.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Prominent Types Disrupt
scenarios.trigger: If Winday or Ascending manage to push forward earlier than mapped and inject pace that fragments the field.
scenarios.body: William Buick's presence on Winday is significant enough that he may force his way closer than the redistribution suggests, compressing the pace and creating a faster gallop that suits an unexposed staying type; however, both Winday and Ascending carry style-fit discounts that make this scenario genuinely unlikely to deliver them as winners.

watchPoints.text: Queenstown's position in running is critical — if Ryan Moore cannot secure the expected second or third spot behind Caballo De Mar due to early crowding from Berkshire Sundance or Winday, the race shape becomes less predictable.

Caballo De Mar's fade-in-finish flag combined with Ascending and Winday being displaced from their natural prominent roles means the early furlongs could be surprisingly contested — monitor how quickly the field settles in the first half-mile.

Berkshire Sundance returns after 42 days and has no confirmed soft-ground form — if the going softens further than Good To Soft before the off, its chance is materially compromised despite strong recent form on Standard surfaces.

Peace Belle and Beylerbeyi are both genuine hold-up types and could be significant players if the pace collapses in the straight — a truly slow tempo over 2m2f on soft ground is the scenario that brings them most into play.

William Buick on Winday is a significant jockey booking for a lightly-raced three-year-old at 122lbs — if Buick elects to push forward rather than accept midfield, this horse could inject unexpected pace and alter the entire race shape.

runners_data.name: Silver Lake
runners_data.note: William Haggas-trained hold-up filly who has won three on the spin including twice on soft, making the going no concern; James Doyle takes the ride and the step up to 1m4f looks a natural progression given her stamina-laden form — 21 days since last run is ideal freshness.
runners_data.comment: Silver Lake arrives in flying form, winning three of her last five starts including back-to-back victories, and she handles today's going with confidence; the stiff weight of 131 lb is the one factor that could blunt her momentum here.

runners_data.name: Salamanca City
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with a strong record at 12f on both soft and good going, and James Fanshawe's yard is operating at a respectable 4/17 over the past fortnight; from a middle draw she can track the pace from midfield and is proven at this level and trip.
runners_data.comment: Salamanca City arrives on the back of a win two starts back and has shown a consistent knack for hitting the frame, with three wins in her last five starts. She has run over today's distance and going before, and at 138 lb she faces a stiff weight task, but her rating of 96 marks her as the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Green Sky
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's six-year-old is the Strand Scorecard selection and brings a genuinely strong profile of three wins at 12-14f on good or better, but the sim-going record of 0W2P on soft is a note of caution that partially tempers confidence; Charlie Tucker's 7lb claim helps the handicapper and the 13-day turnaround suggests she is in good fettle.
runners_data.comment: Green Sky has winning form in her recent starts, scoring three times in her last six, but she arrives here off a third last time out and a fourth two starts back, suggesting she can be inconsistent; distance and going experience both assist her claims at 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Room Fourteen
runners_data.note: Scorecard danger who contests from midfield and has won three of her last five including twice at 10f on good ground for Fanshawe, though all her best form has come on faster surfaces — the 42-day break needs monitoring but Saffie Osborne is an adept pilot for a young filly; the step up to 1m4f is the key unknown.
runners_data.comment: Room Fourteen has a lively recent record with three wins in her last six starts, including back-to-back victories two and three starts back, and she returns third last time out; but ranked ninth of ten on our figures, she faces a stiff ask at the weights here.

runners_data.name: Ruby Wedding
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy on a prominent-running Andrew Balding three-year-old who won at 12f on good and has placed at 12f on standard; the wide draw of 1 is noted but suits a horse likely to be ridden handy, and the Going to Soft represents a query on a filly whose best form is on faster ground.

runners_data.name: Thatwilldoso
runners_data.note: Scorecard danger who races prominently and has won at 10f on good and placed at 12f on good; Kevin Thomas Coleman's yard is 0/11 over the past fortnight which is a cold trainer angle, and the soft-going record of 1W3P from 7-8 runs is competitive without being dominant over this longer trip.
runners_data.comment: Thatwilldoso arrives in decent nick — a winner last time out and a second two starts back — but rated eighth of ten on our figures, she faces a stiff ask against this field, and the drop in form fifth and unplaced efforts earlier in this sequence add to the concern.

runners_data.name: Nochebuena
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Ralph Beckett who has won at 12f on soft, giving her genuine going credentials; the 63-day absence is the primary risk, and she faces a direct pace duel with Golden Muse which may compromise her chance of controlling the race on her own terms.
runners_data.comment: Nochebuena shaped with plenty of promise when runner-up last time out, and her win two starts back underlines she knows how to win; she has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 90 makes her a leading danger — the main concern is her 63-day absence.

runners_data.name: Aequitas
runners_data.note: David O'Meara four-year-old returning after a 307-day layoff, having finished 11th on soft over 14f last time out before that long break — the fitness question is severe and Daniel Tudhope cannot paper over that gap without evidence of strong home work; her one win came on good ground at 12f.
runners_data.comment: Aequitas showed her best when winning back-to-back three and four starts back, and she has the distance-and-going experience to suggest conditions suit; the main concern is a lengthy 307-day absence leaving her match-fitness open to question.

runners_data.name: Golden Muse
runners_data.note: Marco Botti's lightly-raced three-year-old is a confirmed front-runner whose entire winning form (three victories) has come on standard or AW surfaces; the 93-day break and a first start on genuine soft turf are twin uncertainties, and if she is outbattled early by Nochebuena her chance evaporates quickly.
runners_data.comment: A winner last time out and three wins in her last five starts give Golden Muse solid recent form, and she has run over today's trip before; however, a 93-day absence and a competitive field ranking sixth of ten offer reasons for mild caution.

runners_data.name: Bint Al Daar
runners_data.note: Six-year-old for Kevin & Lauren Frost who carries visor headgear and a modest recent form string (1-5-8-7-9-0), with soft-going form that reads 0W0P from 14 runs in similar conditions; Joanna Mason takes the ride but the overall profile of a horse rated 70 in this company is uninspiring.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Bint Al Daar has been unplaced in her last three starts and has managed just one win in her last six, making her hard to fancy despite experience over today's trip and going and a prompt 21-day turnaround.

races.paceDynamic: Nochebuena and Golden Muse are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over this 1m4f trip on Good to Soft ground, creating a genuine, honest gallop rather than a tactical crawl. Nochebuena, drawn 2, will try to assert early, but Golden Muse from draw 10 will push across and apply pressure, meaning neither can fully dictate without a fight — the early sectionals will be genuinely competitive. That contested pace over a stamina trip on softened ground will stretch the field out early, likely burning off those who lack the resolution to sustain a long run, and creating conditions where the closing sectionals are punishing for those who have committed energy up front. This race shape strongly favours hold-up and midfield runners with proven soft-ground stamina who can pick up the pieces in the final two furlongs — horses like Green Sky and Silver Lake are archetypal beneficiaries of this kind of setup.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Reign
scenarios.trigger: If Nochebuena and Golden Muse push each other through a genuine gallop that softens the front two before the home turn.
scenarios.body: The honest early pace on Good to Soft ground saps the leaders' reserves, leaving the race to those tracking from midfield or off the pace who arrive with energy in the tank; the final 2f on Doncaster's flat straight become a stamina test that sorts those with genuine resolution.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Nochebuena establishes a clear early lead, sets a controlled tempo, and Golden Muse fails to sustain her challenge past halfway.
scenarios.body: With the pace dialled back and Nochebuena able to dictate on her own terms, she conserves enough energy to repel challengers in the straight, a profile she has shown before winning over 1m2f on soft; the longer trip and softer ground are the key risks.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind, Hold-Up Blocked
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely fierce but the field bunches in the straight, creating traffic for hold-up horses and allowing prominent stalkers to pounce.
scenarios.body: Ruby Wedding, prominent from draw 1 with Oisin Murphy confident in traffic management, and Thatwilldoso can exploit a position just off the pace and get first run on the hold-up brigade; both have won at this kind of trip and style.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If the ground rides slower than the Good to Soft official description and the race becomes a stamina test that exposes horses without genuine soft-ground form.
scenarios.body: Salamanca City's consistent soft-ground record (wins at 12f on soft) and Room Fourteen's progressive profile off a 42-day break both come into sharp relief; horses with any soft-ground concern or big weights become liabilities in a true slog.

watchPoints.text: Green Sky and Silver Lake are both hold-up types converging on the same race shape — if they meet traffic in the straight, one or both could be denied a clear run despite having the ideal profile for this scenario.

Golden Muse is 93 days off the track and has never raced on genuine soft turf; if she weakens quickly after being outpaced by Nochebuena in the early duel, the pace shape of the race could collapse into a false dawdle rather than the genuine gallop the scenario analysis assumes.

Aequitas returns after 307 days off and finished 11th on soft last time — watch in the paddock and early exchanges for signs of rustiness; if she trails tamely, she can be safely dismissed and the market move should be treated with scepticism.

Room Fourteen has run all her best races at 10f — the jump to 1m4f is untested and if she fades in the final furlong after looking dangerous turning in, the extra two furlongs of soft ground will have found her out.

The Good to Soft official description for the 3:35 is consistent across all races on the card, suggesting conditions are uniform rather than patchy — horses who have thrived specifically on soft rather than good-to-soft may find slightly less advantage than their form implies.

runners_data.name: It Dunt Marra
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a useful second on soft (9/6f/SOF) and a win at 5f on good — handles conditions, but stepping up in quality in a 16-runner handicap; Stevie Donohoe holds the book.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win two starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making It Dunt Marra a genuine threat at 131 lb from stall four; the main concern is a beaten ninth last time out that he must put behind him.

runners_data.name: Pride Of Toledo
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Clive Cox and P J McDonald, with decent soft form; the concern is whether he can avoid getting swamped in a five-way pace battle that may cost him dearly inside the final 2f.
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back and shaped with promise when fourth last time out, Pride Of Toledo has experience of today's trip and conditions and carries his 135 lb well enough; drawn in stall eight, he lines up as the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Bear Lee
runners_data.note: Michael & David Easterby's hold-up performer has a soft-ground win in his recent history (4/6f/SOF) and runs fresh off just 11 days; Joanna Mason will drop in from draw 1 and look to deliver late — the pace shape suits his profile.
runners_data.comment: Bear Lee was a winner four starts back but has since posted three fourth-place finishes and a fifth in recent starts, suggesting consistency without the cutting edge to break through again; she has run over today's trip and returns on a quick 11-day turnaround from stall one carrying 127 lb.

runners_data.name: Washington Royale
runners_data.note: Won on soft most recently (1/6f/SOF) and won at this trip, making him one of the better-credentialled soft-ground performers in the field; Clifford Lee can sit handy and the conditions play to his strengths.
runners_data.comment: Washington Royale won last time out and has experience of today's distance and going, but fifth twice in his last four starts tempers enthusiasm, and 131 lb from stall nine is no light burden for a 75-rated colt returning on a quick 11-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Baddaddan
runners_data.note: Saffie Osborne partners Richard Spencer's two-year-old, who has a win over 6f on good but the 0/0 pattern in soft ground is a question mark; draw 14 is workable but not ideal for a pace-pressed field.
runners_data.comment: Baddaddan makes little appeal on our figures, ranked bottom of the field, and an unplaced run last time out does nothing to encourage, though he does hold distance experience and a win two starts back shows he retains ability.

runners_data.name: Super Tuscan
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's gelding has won at 6f on good and been placed at the trip; Oliver Carmichael's 7lb claim helps the weight, and he should be able to track the pace comfortably from draw 10.
runners_data.comment: Super Tuscan catches the eye with a runner-up finish last time out, 23 days ago, and he has experience over today's trip, while our rating of 91 marks him as a leading contender; the main risk is that five of his last six starts have ended without a win.

runners_data.name: Henley On Thames
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard's top selection at medium confidence — consecutive wins at 6f on good, progressive form string (62211), and David Egan in the saddle for Kevin Philippart De Foy; prominent racer who should travel sweetly off this strong gallop and be produced late.
runners_data.comment: Henley On Thames arrives in decent nick off a 23-day break, back-to-back wins his most recent form, though a sixth two starts beyond those hints at inconsistency; he has run over today's trip before and carries 133 lb from stall 12.

runners_data.name: Launch Sequence
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's charge has been placed twice at 6f on good, James Doyle takes the ride, and the headgear flag suggests he has needed assistance to focus; middle draw suits the midfield style, but the soft may not be his optimum.
runners_data.comment: Third two starts back, and again three starts back, Launch Sequence arrives with experience over today's trip and going, fit on 21 days' rest, with his trainer firing at a 31% strike rate; the risk is that he's yet to win in recent starts and was only sixth last time out.

runners_data.name: Tumishi
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's gelding won last time at 6f on good and has Daniel Muscutt aboard; three runs only so lightly exposed, and the low draw from a prominent position could see him travel keenly into the race.
runners_data.comment: Tumishi won last time out and has run over today's trip, but rated 80 and carrying 130 lb from stall 2, he faces a stiff ask against what looks a competitive field, with only a third two starts back as additional recent encouragement.

runners_data.name: Wait Geordie
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's front-runner has a habit of leading but his form string (138785) reveals consistent decline in competitiveness; longest at 5f mostly, stepping to 6f on soft for the first time is a significant ask, and 37 days off adds uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Wait Geordie showed to good effect with a win and a third in recent starts, but three subsequent efforts of seventh or worse in his last three runs cloud the picture; he has run over today's trip before, and 37 days between runs leaves his current form an open question.

runners_data.name: Beresford Gap
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes over for Andrew Balding from draw 6, and this hold-up type has placed at 6f twice; 50 days since last run is the only concern, but Murphy's tactical intelligence makes him well-placed to exploit any pace collapse from the lead.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked 13 of 16 on our figures, Beresford Gap heads into this off a 50-day absence with little in the way of encouragement, though he has run over today's trip before and placed efforts of late offer a sliver of consolation.

runners_data.name: Sir Sirius
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's runner tries to go forward from draw 13, which creates an awkward wide-to-cross scenario in a full field; Tom Eaves will need a clean break, and the 78-day absence makes him a harder proposition in this company.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and returning after 78 days off, Sir Sirius does at least have distance experience to call on and a third last time out offers some encouragement, though carrying 125 lb from stall 13 while ranked 11 of 16 suggests he faces a stiff task here.

runners_data.name: Innichen
runners_data.note: Jack Channon's horse has won twice — both at 5f — and has a soft-ground blot (19th at Doncaster); Tom Marquand will use the hold-up style, but the soft and 6f combination needs answering before confidence can be high.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and a winner twice in his last six starts, Innichen brings solid recent form and has run over today's trip, though an unplaced effort in that sequence tempers expectations; he carries 135 lb from stall 11 and our rating of 88 suggests he is competitive here.

runners_data.name: Sue's Last Chance
runners_data.note: Another confirmed front-runner for Fahey, but the headgear flag and a form string of 6580 on good make this a pace contributor rather than a likely winning force; Barry McHugh will push forward but she may be swamped by superior rivals.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked 14 of 16 on our figures, Sue's Last Chance makes little appeal, though he has run over today's trip and returns after a reasonable 23-day break from stall 3 carrying 122 lb.

runners_data.name: Fasthope
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's runner won at 6f on good and has soft-ground placed form; a natural prominent/prominent racer by inclination who is unlikely to secure that berth in this congested pace scenario — the STYLE_FIT flag tempers expectations, and draw 15 makes early position even harder to claim.
runners_data.comment: Beaten well into eighth last time out, and ranked bottom two of the field on our figures, Fasthope is hard to fancy despite a win two starts back and the experience of today's trip and going in his favour.

runners_data.name: Fern Clyde
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's progressive sort has won at 6f and carries headgear; by nature a front-running/prominent type pushed into a midfield slot by pace congestion — draw 16 is the widest in the field, making it extremely unlikely she can cross and assert her preferred role, so discount the chance accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 12 of 16 on our figures, Fern Clyde is hard to fancy here, finishing sixth last time out and fourth two starts back, though she does have experience over today's trip and going and a win four starts back offers some encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Pride Of Toledo, Wait Geordie, Beresford Gap, Sir Sirius, and Sue's Last Chance all break from the gates with lead intentions, guaranteeing a genuinely strong gallop over 6f on Good To Soft ground — a pace shape that will stretch stamina and almost certainly compromise the front-runners themselves before the furlong pole. With five horses seeking the same position, the early fractions will be fierce, burning energy that creates a strong tailwind for horses tracking behind the pace rather than setting it. The tactical verdict is clear: prominent-to-midfield horses who can travel smoothly off a contested pace and produce a sustained late run will be the primary beneficiaries — particularly those with soft-ground form and a finishing kick rather than raw early speed. The field contains more prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — Fern Clyde and Fasthope are genuine front-running/prominent horses by inclination but are most likely to be outgunned for early position, with Pride Of Toledo, Beresford Gap, and Sir Sirius most likely to actually secure a lead berth.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace collapse, closers pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the five front-runners burn each other out inside 3f and the field strings out, setting up a strong-staying finisher.
scenarios.body: The contested lead will see early splits unsustainably quick for soft ground over 6f, and horses who travel mid-to-rear will be delivered late with reserves intact; Henley On Thames fits this profile perfectly, having won his last two over the trip, while Bear Lee's hold-up style from a low draw is tailor-made.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent horse survives
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner breaks cleanly and crosses to a rail, dictating a comfortable lead while rivals neutralise each other.
scenarios.body: A single horse that finds an uncontested lead — likely Beresford Gap with Oisin Murphy's tactical acumen from a middle-low draw — could exploit the chaos behind and control tempo just enough to hold on; Henley On Thames remains dangerous but a clean escape makes this harder to reel in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield deliver late surge
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is strong but not suicidal and two or three prominent types stalk the pace and kick clear in the final 2f.
scenarios.body: Henley On Thames and Super Tuscan, both proven at this trip and comfortable on give underfoot, have the tactical position to be produced with a run as the leaders crack; this scenario suits horses with a genuine middle-stage cruising speed rather than pure finishing speed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, outsider lands it
scenarios.trigger: If the pace completely implodes and a lightly-raced or improving type seizes an unexpected gap through a disorganised field.
scenarios.body: Washington Royale's recent soft-ground win and Tumishi's course-form at this trip could see one of these profit from a race that falls apart in front of them; Baddaddan, with a fast-ground win at the trip, is less well-suited but would be live if this turns into a sprint from the front half.

watchPoints.text: Five confirmed front-runners (Pride Of Toledo, Wait Geordie, Beresford Gap, Sir Sirius, Sue's Last Chance) are all drawn within a 13-stall range — watch the first 2f for a pace battle that could blow the race apart and hand it to those tracking off the speed.

Sir Sirius breaks from draw 13 as a confirmed front-runner — if he has to cross the field to lead, he will either use significant energy or be checked, both outcomes degrading his chance and potentially causing interference.

Fern Clyde (draw 16) and Fasthope (draw 15) are natural prominent types on the outside who are highly unlikely to secure their preferred position — if either burns energy trying to claim a forward berth, their finishing effort will be materially compromised.

Bear Lee has run just 11 days ago — watch for signs at the start whether the quick turnaround has left her fresh or flat; Joanna Mason will know, and an early show of keenness or reluctance will signal which way it goes.

Innichen's Doncaster blot (19th, 6f, soft) came on soft ground at this exact course and trip — if the ground is riding on the testing side of Good To Soft, that entry in his form should not be overlooked when assessing his true ability in conditions.
