runners_data.name: Almekarem
runners_data.note: Lightly weighted Sir Mark Prescott runner who has won on soft and is in cracking recent form (won 11 days ago), operating from a neutral draw 12; genuine midfield operator who should travel within the pace and pose a late threat if the strong gallop plays out as expected.
runners_data.comment: Almekarem has placed in back-to-back runs and a win four starts back gives him a decent recent profile, though a seventh three starts back is the blot; he has run over today's trip and going, returns fit on 11 days, and a yard firing at 26% gives him every chance from stall 12 off 142 lb.

runners_data.name: Amidst The Chaos
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler hold-up runner whose best sim-going effort came over 12f on Flat, but form figures on cut ground are limited; Rowan Scott takes over and the horse must travel from draw 10, though a lack of soft-ground wins is a flag.
runners_data.comment: Ranked a long way down the field on our figures and drawn in stall ten, Amidst The Chaos faces a stiff ask, with his trainer returning just one winner from twenty-two runners in the last fortnight; he has run over today's trip and returns on a quick turnaround, but that is modest consolation.

runners_data.name: Optician
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard selection — won over 12f on soft at Yarmouth and has course-relevant experience; Michael Herrington's gelding operates from a midfield position and draw 16 suits in a scenario where closers are delivered wide and late on a flat track; confidence tagged low but the profile fits the expected race shape well.
runners_data.comment: Optician showed he can win in recent starts, with a second two starts back adding further encouragement, but a ninth last time out clouds his claims; he has run over today's trip and going, and carries 136 lb from stall 16 after a 25-day absence.

runners_data.name: Without Compromise
runners_data.note: Antony Brittain's prominent-racing five-year-old has shown solid placed form including a second at 10f, and Cam Hardie from draw 5 can find a handy pitch without fighting for the lead; the trip looks adequate but the soft going is not tested.
runners_data.comment: Without Compromise has shown he can mix it at this level — a second two starts back offers encouragement — but a sixth last time out and winless in his last five starts give pause; has run over today's trip and arrives on a handy 26-day break, though his rating of 78 leaves him mid-pack in a competitive field.

runners_data.name: Reveur
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's lightly raced three-year-old with a 126-day absence is a significant unknown — going preference is unestablished and this trip on soft ground for a horse returning from a long layoff asks many questions; Daniel Tudhope's booking is a positive but the risk rating is high.
runners_data.comment: Reveur showed he has the ability to win when successful four starts back, and with a lengthy absence of 126 days now behind him, he arrives relatively unexposed and open to further progress carrying 132 lb from stall one.

runners_data.name: Everyoneknowsadave
runners_data.note: Jessica Macey's progressive four-year-old has won at 10f and placed multiple times in this sphere; Sean Levey rides from draw 6 which allows a handy position, and soft ground has not been tested but the recent form figures (2,1,4,2,3) scream consistency over this sort of trip.
runners_data.comment: Everyoneknowsadave filled the runner-up spot last time out and has experience of today's distance and going, but he was fourth two starts back and has managed only one win in his last six starts, making him a tough nut to crack from stall 6 off 137 lb.

runners_data.name: His Finest Hour
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason partners this Tina Jackson-trained five-year-old who has placed twice on soft ground and shaped with credit at 11f on Flat; a hold-up runner by nature who would need the pace to be genuine, and from draw 14 should find a clean passage on the outside.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last five starts, His Finest Hour at least brings strong place consistency — second and third among those efforts — and has run over today's trip and going before; 133 lb from stall 14 is the counterweight, though a return to form isn't out of the question.

runners_data.name: Director's Cut
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner from draw 11 who is running off a 74-day break; wears a p-headgear flag suggesting he can be keen, and stepping up to 12f from his usual 8-10f range is unproven — likely to be one of the horses whose pace contribution helps others more than himself if he tires.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well held on our figures in a 19-runner field, Director's Cut arrives unplaced last time out and has mustered only one win in his last five starts, making him hard to fancy. He has run over today's trip before and 131 lb is workable, but the case for him is slim.

runners_data.name: Canvas
runners_data.note: Races to lead and flags as a horse who fades in the finish — a genuine concern in a soft-ground stamina test over 1m2f where five want the same early real estate; from draw 7 he will press forward but may be a casualty of the pace war he helps create.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Canvas nonetheless catches the eye on profile, stepping back up to familiar distance and going conditions, and he arrives fit on just a five-day turnaround; second last time out lifts the spirits, though the trainer's current run of form is a note of caution.

runners_data.name: Something Splendid
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard danger — Tom Marquand partners this Peter Chapple-Hyam four-year-old who has won twice on soft/good-to-soft and showed a win last time out at 10f on soft; prominent style from draw 2 means he can take a forward position without over-exerting, and the profile aligns with a strong-pace scenario where a settled prominent horse outstays the true front-runners.
runners_data.comment: Something Splendid won last time out but that sits alongside three poor efforts in his last four starts before it, and ranked 13 of 19 on our figures he faces a stiff ask here, though he has run over today's trip and going and returns on a fresh enough 12-day break.

runners_data.name: Newtown Duke
runners_data.note: Ian Williams-trained five-year-old fitted with a t-headgear flag, returning from 90 days off; has placed twice on soft including a third at 12f, which is the most directly relevant piece of evidence here — a genuine hold-up type who could stay on without threatening the market leaders.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and a winner three starts back, Newtown Duke has reasonable claims on form but his trainer's poor recent strike-rate and a 90-day absence are real concerns; he has run over today's trip and going, which at least counts in his favour.

runners_data.name: Amancio
runners_data.note: Tom Eaves partners Faye Bramley's prominent-racing five-year-old who has won twice on soft ground, including at 17f and 9f — the soft-ground record is strong; fitted with a t-headgear flag and returning from 75 days off, the big question is whether the layoff blunts his readiness after a promising pre-break run.
runners_data.comment: Amancio franked his recent form with a win last time out and has experience of both today's trip and the going, with his official mark of 79 looking workable off stall four; the main concern is the 75-day absence since that victory.

runners_data.name: Highland Olly
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner who has never won on soft ground across 13 qualifying runs; Grant Tuer's five-year-old from draw 15 will race prominently on the outside, contributing to the hot early fractions but likely to pay for it in the stamina test — the going record is a meaningful concern.
runners_data.comment: Highland Olly has struggled for consistency in recent starts, finishing seventh and fifth in his last two before rallying to third last time out, and his rating of 75 ranks him fourteenth of nineteen here, making him difficult to fancy despite having run over today's trip.

runners_data.name: On The Inlet
runners_data.note: Another confirmed pace-setter, a three-year-old trained by Dr Richard Newland and Jamie Insole from draw 13; won over 7f earlier this year and has been running over 8-10f, so 12f on soft is a significant step up in both trip and ground — likely to be prominent but may not last home.
runners_data.comment: On The Inlet brings solid recent form — third last time out and third two starts back — and has run over today's trip and going, with a rating of 82 supporting his claims; however, he carries 132 lb from stall 13 and has been out of the placings in two of his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Fans Favourite
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy rides this Hugo Palmer three-year-old who has won three times on soft ground and is clearly suited by give underfoot; a hold-up runner fitted with a p-headgear flag, the 3W3P soft record is the standout statistic and from draw 17 Murphy can be produced with a wide late run.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well adrift of the field on our figures and drawn in stall 17, Fans Favourite is hard to fancy despite a lively recent record that includes wins in his last six starts, most recently a winner thirteen days ago, and experience over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Illy's Roo
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's David Egan-partnered three-year-old from draw 19 has a modest sim-going record of 0W0P but has won over 8f on good ground; the hold-up style from the widest draw on a flat course is not ideal in a big field, and she may find herself covering too much ground.
runners_data.comment: Illy's Roo was a winner four starts back but has disappointed in his last three outings, including a ninth last time out just five days ago, leaving his form under a cloud; he has run over today's going before and a mark of 77 gives him something to work with.

runners_data.name: Spirit Genie
runners_data.note: Jason Hart takes over on this Jennie Candlish six-year-old who won last time out over 8f on Good; fitted with a tb-headgear combination and holds up in the field, but the step up to 12f and a 37-day break after a course win are factors — soft ground has produced modest placed form only (0W1P).
runners_data.comment: Spirit Genie arrives on the back of a win, handles today's distance and going, and a rating of 85 has him firmly in contention from stall three; the main concern is that unplaced run sandwiched between his recent efforts, hinting at inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Ziata
runners_data.note: Saffie Osborne rides Gemma Tutty's three-year-old front-runner from draw 18; has a soft-ground record of 5 runs for 0W1P and steps up in trip — a horse likely to feature prominently early but who will be caught in the crossfire of a five-way pace battle from an outside draw.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 18 of 19 on our figures, Ziata faces a stiff task, and a sixth and an unplaced run in her last two starts do little to inspire confidence, though she has run over today's trip and going before and a win three starts back shows she can find the line.

runners_data.name: Naples
runners_data.note: PJ McDonald on Steph Hollinshead's hold-up four-year-old fitted with a p-headgear flag; the form figures (0,0,3,5,0 recent) are largely poor and recent soft-going experience is not encouraging — this is a horse who may need a very specific set of circumstances to threaten.
runners_data.comment: Rated highest in the field and winless in recent starts, Naples brings distance-and-going experience and a lively fitness edge at 26 days since his last run, with his third three starts back offering a form pointer — though he must convert that promise under 134 lb from stall nine.

races.paceDynamic: Highland Olly, On The Inlet, Director's Cut, Canvas, and Ziata all want to lead or race prominently, guaranteeing a strong, honest gallop from the off over 1m2f on Good to Soft ground at Doncaster — a track that already stretches stamina on its long straight. With five front-runners fighting for supremacy, the pace will be relentless early, stretching the field and draining the leaders' reserves, setting up a searching test that will heavily favour those who can be produced with a run from off the pace. The mid-to-rear section — Optician, Almekarem, Fans Favourite, Something Splendid — are structurally best placed to absorb the strong gallop and arrive late with untapped reserves. The tactical verdict is unambiguous: this race shape strongly favours genuine hold-up and midfield runners who can travel within themselves and pick off tying leaders in the final two furlongs; front-runners are likely to be compromised by their own pace battle.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace, Closers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the five pace-setters tear into each other early and the gallop is truly relentless, burning out even the more tractable prominent types.
scenarios.body: The leaders set a searching tempo that leaves them vulnerable inside the final two furlongs, allowing horses held up or racing midfield to reel them in on a stamina-testing surface; Good to Soft conditions amplify the advantage for those who conserve energy early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Quicken Late
scenarios.trigger: If one or two prominent runners settle just off the pace rather than scrapping for the lead, arriving with enough in reserve to quicken past tired front-runners.
scenarios.body: Something Splendid, who has already won twice on soft-ish ground and returns in good form, and Everyoneknowsadave could slot into a prominent but comfortable position and prove best of those with an early pitch; the genuine front-runners burn each other out while these two coast in behind.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Leader Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners fail to truly scorch the early pace and one of them — most likely Director's Cut or On The Inlet — settles into a controlled rhythm and steals a march turning in.
scenarios.body: A moderate gallop would allow a savvy pace-setter to dictate terms at a sustainable clip, with enough left in the locker to fend off a tired midfield who have not been given the right cues to quicken; on a flat track with no bend drama, an unchallenged leader could prove elusive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Fail to Reach
scenarios.trigger: If the pace paradoxically steadies after an early flurry and the midfield-to-rear runners find themselves with too much ground to make up in a short home straight burst.
scenarios.body: Horses deepest in the pack — Naples, Illy's Roo, Amidst The Chaos — would lack the acceleration to bridge the gap if the pace is not truly honest throughout; this scenario suits a resolute stayer who gets daylight early and grinds rather than sprints.

watchPoints.text: Five confirmed front-runners (Highland Olly, On The Inlet, Director's Cut, Canvas, Ziata) will contest every early yard — watch for one burning too bright and stopping dramatically inside the final quarter mile, potentially compromising runners directly behind them.

Fans Favourite's 3W3P soft-ground record is the most compelling going-specific angle in the race; watch whether Oisin Murphy can deliver him from draw 17 with a clean outside passage rather than getting trapped in traffic.

Optician is the Strand Scorecard selection at low confidence — watch draw 16 carefully at the start; if Conor Whiteley (5lb claim) settles him promptly and tracks the pace from a wide midfield position, the 1W on soft and the trip profile align, but a slow start from high draw would be costly.

Something Splendid must nail his prominent position from draw 2 without being dragged into the pace battle — Tom Marquand's key task is to sit just off the leaders without fighting Canvas and Highland Olly; if he is forced to race keenly early, his chance diminishes quickly.

Reveur (126-day absence, going unknown, lightly raced three-year-old) is the most opaque runner in the field — Daniel Tudhope's booking suggests connections are hopeful, but until this horse produces evidence on soft ground over this trip the risk profile is high and it is one to monitor rather than rely upon.
